description: Body-operation identity outcomes (SPEC-v1 §6.0.3, §6.0.5 as ruled by [W0-39] `modified`, [W0-40] `removed` and [W0-41] contacts, degenerate pieces and the smallest cut, with [R-3] coincidence first; and the per-tool failure row of the §6.0.3 table for joins). Each case is a valid `aicad.ir/1` document and, per feature id, the expected `status` and either the error `code` or: `bodies` (the multiset of `{ origin, change }` of the feature entry), `removed` (origins, in any order) and `warnings` (the set of the oracle-computable semantic warning codes of §8.2 the entry must carry; engine-prefixed notes are not compared). Features not listed are not checked; `rule` and `note` are informative. Shared by Forge (forge-ir tests/v1_conformance_amendments.rs, through forge-regen) and the oracle (W7b).

cases.note: k1 overlaps the target e1; k2 overlaps only k1 (8 mm from e1): a tool that neither overlaps nor shares a face with any target is BOOLEAN_NO_INTERSECTION, whatever the other tools do
the tool's face lies 8e-7 mm inside the target's x = 5 face: within tol, the faces coincide (coincidence first), so the overlap is no volume
as above at 9.5e-7 mm (an overlap of exactly tol is not pinned: 10 - 1e-6 is not exact in binary64)
beyond tol the faces are distinct: the cut removes a 2e-6 mm layer
a join tool overlapping by 8e-7 mm shares a face with its target (coincident within tol): joined
the cut leaves an 8e-7 mm layer at x = -5: within tol of the tool's face, it is a contact, not a piece
the tool spans x in [-5 + 8e-7, 0]: the layer at x = -5 is no piece, so one piece remains and there is no split
tool k1 overlaps the target's top by 3e-7 mm (a contact) and tool k2, touching k1, is a 0.01 mm pocket: the pocket is cut; the contact is never averaged with it
the same slab and pocket joined into one tool body first: the common part is one connected sliver-and-pocket, and the pocket is still cut

the target's corner (5, 5, 10) lies 2e-6 mm inside a tool bounded by a plane of normal (1, 1, 1): a cut, although the common part (a tetrahedron) has 2V/A = 4.9e-7 <= tol/2; degeneracy is judged on result pieces only

the cut keeps only the prism x + y >= 10 - 1.56e-6 at the corner: its edge is 1.1e-6 mm from the cut face (a real piece), but its mean thickness 2V/A = 4.6e-7 <= tol/2: degenerate, so the target is consumed
the same with legs 3e-6 mm: 2V/A = 8.8e-7 > tol/2, a 4.5e-11 mm^3 body is produced (no threshold relative to s)
the target's vertical edge at (5, 5) lies 8e-7 mm inside the tool's oblique face x + y = 10 - 1.13e-6: within tol it lies on that face, so no point of the target is inside the tool beyond tol

the slit's walls are 1.5e-6 mm apart, more than tol: distinct faces, so the target is cut in two, although no target point is farther than tol from the tool's boundary (the one-sided depth the withdrawn wording of [W0-41] step 2 measured)
as above at the top of the band (tol, 2 tol]
a join tool 1.5e-6 mm thin inside the target meets it (its mid-plane is farther than tol from the target's faces): the target is modified, not BOOLEAN_NO_INTERSECTION
a cut tool 1.5e-6 mm thin inside the target meets it: the target is modified (a closed void whose walls are distinct faces)

the target's corner (5, 5, 10) lies 1.2e-6 mm inside a tool bounded by a plane of normal (1, 1, 1): farther than tol from the tool's face, so a cut, although the common tetrahedron's inscribed ball is only 8.8e-7 mm across (2V/A = 2.9e-7): thickness is the distance to the faces, not an inscribed-ball measure
a 1.5e-6 mm square pin through the target cuts a through-hole whose opposite walls are distinct faces

the fin's two walls are 1.5e-6 mm apart, more than tol, and each coincides with a tool face: every point of the fin is within tol of a target face and of a tool face, but the fin contains a ball 1.5e-6 mm across, so T ∩ K is volume and the cut removes the fin (under [W0-48]'s face-distance test alone it was a contact: BOOLEAN_NO_INTERSECTION)

the cut leaves a 10 x 10 mm wall 1.5e-6 mm thick between the target's x = 5 face and the tool's x = 5 - 1.5e-6 face: its faces are distinct, it contains a ball 1.5e-6 mm across (not a layer), and its mean thickness 2V/A is about 1.5e-6 mm > tol/2 (not degenerate), so the target is modified, not consumed
